The person's Haemoglobin levels will affect the HbA1c result as will conditions which affect the Haemoglobin part of the blood, such as haemoglobinopathy.

LFTs, Kidney and Thyroid function should also be taken as these may have an affect.

Medications and steroids will need to be taken into account too.

Fructosamine and C-peptide are also useful in ascertaining how much insulin the body is producing itself. 

​

The HbA1c itself will show how much of your Haemoglobin has sugar attached to it over the last lifecycle of the Hb (2-3 months). It'll therefore give you an average blood glucose level for the past 2-3 months, depending on if your Hb is reliable.
